headlines.title: Map: Track the spread of measles in the U.S.
headlines.description: NBC News is tracking confirmed measles case counts and state infection tallies. This data will be updated regularly.

headlines.title: Is the Secret to a Healthy Relationship a Good Fight?
headlines.description: Conflict can actually deepen relationships, so Priya Parker, author of “The Art of Fighting,” stops by TODAY to talk about how to improve connections through productive fighting. She discusses misconceptions about conflict, how to “argue nicely,” and more.

headlines.title: Social Media Health Trends: What’s Real and What’s Not?
headlines.description: It’s hard to know what advice on social media is legitimate, especially when it comes to health and wellness. NBC news medical reporter Dr. Akshay Syal joins TODAY to break down social media health trends, including dry scooping a pre-workout powder, eating more sardines, drinking tart cherry juice for sleep and more.

headlines.title: How to Do the Real Work of Self-Healing and Address Negativity
headlines.description: The journey of self-healing can be overwhelming, so licensed therapist and author Kier Gaines joins TODAY to share some tips from his new book “It All Starts When You Do: How to Do the Real Work of Self-Healing.” He discusses common misconceptions when it comes to healing, how to address negative self-messaging, and more.

headlines.title: Teen Learns to Walk Again After Accident, Now Running Track
headlines.description: After a life-threatening sledding accident at age 6 that left him with a traumatic brain injury, Bensten Schone faced a long and grueling road to recovery. But he refused to let it define his life, learning to breathe, walk and talk again. The now-high school senior is defying the odds by running track. “I love a comeback story, and when they said they didn’t think I could walk again, I was determined to walk and maybe run,” Bensten said. TODAY's Craig Melvin shares his story.

headlines.title: It’s now illegal to touch your phone while driving in some states — here’s how to stay compliant
headlines.description: More than 30 states now have hands-free phone laws banning handheld cell phone use while driving. See if your state made the list, what the penalties are and the best products to help you stay compliant.

headlines.title: We’ve tested hundreds of oral care products — these 50 are the most effective
headlines.description: We tested popular and lesser known toothpastes, whitening strips, water flossers and other oral care products to find the 50 best of the year.

headlines.title: The best screen protectors to save your phone and other devices from costly damage
headlines.description: The best screen protectors can shield your phone from scratches, cracks or even shattering. We spoke with repair experts about how they work and the best ones to buy

headlines.title: We found the fluffiest and softest bath towels on Amazon
headlines.description: Design experts share top tips for shopping for bath towels, plus highly rated towels on Amazon to buy now.

headlines.title: When is it safe to return home after a wildfire? California becomes first state to pass standards
headlines.description: California is poised to become the first U.S. state to set standards for testing and remediation for smoke contamination from wildfires, with a pair of bills passed Monday.

headlines.title: Her son fed goats at a petting zoo. He might’ve been exposed to rabies.
headlines.description: Three baby goats at a North Carolina petting zoo tested positive for rabies, sparking a statewide effort to track down everyone who interacted with the animals.

headlines.title: Four baby goats at mobile petting zoo in North Carolina test positive for rabies
headlines.description: Four baby goats from a North Carolina mobile petting zoo tested positive for rabies and were euthanized, and health officials are asking anyone who may have had contact with them to reach out for possible treatment.
